Check for a different installed headless coding CLI, starting with the preferred pairing above.\n3. Discover that reviewer's documented headless and resume flags with `--help` if needed.\n4. Start one persistent reviewer session for the plan/spec artifact when the reviewer supports resumable sessions.\n5. Run the first review in headless mode and capture the session id or thread handle when available.\n6. For later passes, resume that same reviewer session instead of starting fresh when possible.\n7. Give the reviewer the artifact path, relevant user goal, constraints, and a focused review prompt.\n8. Ask the reviewer not to edit files.\n9. Incorporate useful feedback into the plan/spec.\n10. Ignore feedback that is wrong, out of scope, or inconsistent with user instructions.\n11. Rerun the reviewer after material revisions.\n12. Stop when the reviewer says the artifact is ready, or after five total review passes.\n\nIf five passes still leave concerns, proceed with the best available artifact. Do not keep looping.\n\n## Harness Discovery\n\nUse `command -v` or the platform equivalent to check for reviewer CLIs before choosing a fallback. Do not install a new harness just for a second opinion unless the user asks.\n\nTypical checks:\n\n```bash\ncommand -v claude || true\ncommand -v codex || true\ncommand -v gemini || true\ncommand -v opencode || true\n```\n\nPrefer read-only or plan-mode permissions for the reviewer. The reviewer should inspect and comment, not mutate files.\n\n## Claude Code Pattern\n\nFor Claude Code, discover the current flags with `claude --help`. Common headless usage is:\n\n```bash\nclaude -p \"$(cat /tmp/second-opinion-prompt.txt)\" > /tmp/second-opinion-pass-1.txt\n```\n\nIf the installed Claude Code version exposes resume/session flags, use them for later passes. Otherwise, include the previous review summary and revised artifact path in the next headless prompt.\n\n## Codex CLI Pattern\n\nFor Codex, prefer a non-ephemeral session so it can be resumed:\n\n```bash\ncodex exec -C \"$PWD\" --sandbox read-only --json -o /tmp/second-opinion-pass-1.txt -\n```\n\nCapture the session id from the JSONL event stream when available. Resume the same reviewer:\n\n```bash\ncodex exec resume \"$SESSION_ID\" -o /tmp/second-opinion-pass-N.txt -\n```\n\nIf the CLI version exposes a different headless/resume shape, follow that version's `--help` output.\n\n## Gemini CLI Pattern\n\nFor Gemini, prefer non-interactive prompt mode with plan/read-only approval when available:\n\n```bash\ngemini --prompt \"$(cat /tmp/second-opinion-prompt.txt)\" --approval-mode plan --output-format text > /tmp/second-opinion-pass-1.txt\n```\n\nResume the same session with `--resume` if that is available and useful for later passes.\n\n## Review Prompt Template\n\n```text\nYou are my second-opinion planning reviewer. Review the artifact below without editing files.\n\nArtifact: [absolute path]\nUser goal: [brief goal]\nContext and constraints:\n- [important constraints, user preferences, repo defaults]\n\nPlease judge whether this plan/spec is ready to use.\n\nLook for:\n- missing requirements or user instructions,\n- vague tasks, placeholders, fake components, mocks, or fallback behavior posing as final work,\n- scope creep or non-obvious product decisions that need user confirmation,\n- missing file map, ownership, state, persistence, instrumentation, error, or verification details,\n- sequencing problems or tasks that are too large to execute safely,\n- test gaps and unclear acceptance criteria.\n\nReturn:\n1. Verdict: READY or HARDEN\n2. Highest-impact findings, with concrete fixes\n3. Anything you would deliberately leave alone\n```\n\n## Handling Feedback\n\nTreat the reviewer as advisory, not authoritative. Apply feedback when it improves correctness, completeness, clarity, safety, or testability. Do not apply feedback that conflicts with the user, local repo instructions, or already-approved scope.\n\nThe reviewer feedback does not need to be copied into the plan or spec. Keep the durable artifact clean unless the user explicitly asks for review notes.\n\n## Failure Mode\n\nIf no different headless coding harness is available, say that explicitly and use the current harness headlessly if possible. Same-harness review still satisfies the required second-opinion gate when it runs as a separate reviewer session. The first supported routed model is `gpt-5.6-sol`, with the exact Claude Code behavior requested by the user, while the design remains model-agnostic.\n\nThe resulting experience must not require a shell alias, global environment changes, or edits to the user's Claude Code configuration. Native Claude models must keep working unchanged.\n\n## Product outcome\n\nIn Settings > Agents, a user can:\n\n1. Open the provider's ChatGPT/Codex sign-in flow and see when it completes.\n4. Discover models from the service and add a model ID manually.\n5. See those models in the existing Claude Code model picker.\n6. Start, resume, prewarm, and recover Claude Code workers with the selected routed model.\n\nFor `gpt-5.6-sol`, OmniHarness launches Claude Code with behavior equivalent to:\n\n```sh\nCLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \\\nCLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1 \\\nCLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY=3 \\\nENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false \\\nclaude --model gpt-5.6-sol\n```\n\nThe ACP adapter is launched by OmniHarness, so the main `--model` choice is represented by `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol`. The gateway connection is injected only into that worker process.\n\n## Scope\n\n### Included\n\n- Managed download, checksum verification, configuration, start, stop, restart adoption, and status for CLIProxyAPI.\n- External-service mode for users who already run CLIProxyAPI.\n- Provider OAuth URL creation and completion polling through CLIProxyAPI's management API.\n- Model discovery from the Anthropic-compatible service plus user-defined model IDs.\n- Routed-model entries in the existing Claude Code model picker.\n- Exact environment construction for all Claude worker creation paths.\n- Persistence, secret handling, named lifecycle events, explicit error surfaces, internationalized UI, deterministic tests, and a real local smoke test.\n\n### Not included in this milestone\n\n- Uninstalling CLIProxyAPI or deleting its credentials.\n- Automatic upgrades or background release checks after installation.\n- Editing shell profiles, creating aliases, or modifying global Claude settings.\n- Running CLIProxyAPI on a non-loopback interface in managed mode.\n- Supporting arbitrary Anthropic-compatible gateways with different management APIs. External mode still expects the CLIProxyAPI-compatible data plane; OAuth controls require its management API.\n- Silent fallback from a routed model to a native Claude model.\n\n## Existing architecture and integration points\n\n- Settings are persisted in SQLite. Keys recognized as secrets are encrypted and are omitted from normal settings GET responses.\n- Every Claude worker eventually uses `spawnAgent()` or `prewarmWorker()` in `src/server/bridge-client/index.ts`, but the base environment is currently read independently at many callers. Implementation must make the bridge functions invoke one routed-model preparation helper themselves, then audit every caller; it must not assume the existing environment reads are centralized.\n- The agent runtime starts `claude-agent-acp`; it does not currently apply the selected Claude model.\n- Worker pool fingerprints already include `ANTHROPIC_*` and `CLAUDE_*` variables, so a routed model can safely receive a distinct process pool.\n- The agents catalog is the source for the composer model picker.\n- `src/server/agent-runtime/manager.ts`, `src/server/bridge-client/index.ts`, and `src/app/home/useHomeMutations.ts` are already large. The integration must be implemented in focused modules and use those files only as delegation points.\n- Server lifecycle decisions must follow `docs/architecture/lifecycle-observability-and-testing.md`.\n- Quota resume currently reconstructs a worker from run-level preferred model/account/effort. That is insufficient once actual worker routing can differ, so the effective launch selection must also be persisted on each worker and used for every resume/recovery path.\n- `src/server/restart-control.ts` and `src/server/dev/bridge-lock.ts` already provide injected process operations, liveness checks, PID records, and command-identity validation patterns. Extract their portable liveness/PID/command-query pieces into one shared process-ownership module and refactor the existing consumers to it. Do not reuse `createNodeRestartSystem().spawnDetached()` for the gateway because its shell/PTY logging pipeline is app-restart-specific; the gateway launches the binary directly with file descriptors and an argument array.\n\n## Model identity\n\nPersisted model selections need to distinguish a native Claude model from a raw gateway model ID. OmniHarness will use an internal route prefix:\n\n```text\ncliproxyapi:gpt-5.6-sol\n```\n\n`encodeClaudeGatewayModel(rawId)` and `decodeClaudeGatewayModel(selection)` are the only code paths allowed to construct or interpret this value. The raw ID is sent to Claude Code; the encoded value remains in runs, worker preferences, and UI state.\n\nThis prevents a gateway outage from accidentally turning `gpt-5.6-sol` into a native Claude request. Existing native values such as `claude-sonnet-*` remain untouched.\n\n## Settings and durable state\n\nThe SQLite settings table remains authoritative. New stable settings are:\n\n| Key | Meaning | Secret |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_MODE` | `managed` or `external` | No |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_ENABLED` | Whether managed service should run and restart | No |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` | Loopback managed URL or external URL | No |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_API_TOKEN` | Data-plane bearer token | Yes |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Management API bearer token | Yes |\n| `CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_MODELS` | JSON list of custom model IDs and optional labels | No |\n| `__CLAUDE_MODEL_GATEWAY_CATALOG_CACHE` | Last valid discovery result, source, and timestamp | Internal |\n\nManaged binaries and credentials live outside the repository under `~/.omniharness/cliproxyapi/`:\n\n```text\nversions/<version>/<binary>\nmanaged-config.yaml\nauth/\nprocess.json\nlogs/\n```\n\nDirectories containing credentials are mode `0700`; config, metadata containing secrets, and log files are mode `0600`. Secrets never appear in API status payloads, events, error messages, command arguments, or test snapshots.\n\nInstallation is retryable. Generated secrets are persisted in a provisional disabled state before filesystem or process operations. The same values are reused on retry. `enabled=true` is written only after readiness succeeds.\n\nManaged files carry an OmniHarness ownership marker. If a target path exists without that marker, the operation refuses instead of overwriting it. Stop never deletes files or credentials.\n\n## Managed installation\n\nThe installer follows this order:\n\n1. Detect `cli-proxy-api` or `cliproxyapi` already on `PATH` and record it as the managed executable without copying it.\n2. Otherwise request the latest official CLIProxyAPI GitHub release.\n3. Select a supported asset for macOS, Linux, or Windows on `x64` or `arm64`.\n4. Download the archive and published checksum file to a version-scoped temporary location.\n5. Its process adapter uses the shared process-ownership primitives extracted from restart control and bridge locking, while its child launch is a direct `spawn(executable, args, { shell: false, stdio })`. It maintains:\n\n- a monotonically increasing status revision;\n- one in-flight operation per operation kind;\n- executable/config/PID ownership metadata;\n- bounded stdout/stderr tails with redaction;\n- readiness and liveness probes;\n- shutdown handlers that stop only a verified owned child.\n\nThe managed command is equivalent to:\n\n```sh\ncli-proxy-api --config ~/.omniharness/cliproxyapi/managed-config.yaml\n```\n\nThe generated configuration binds only to `127.0.0.1`, defaults to port `8317`, uses the managed auth directory, and contains randomly generated data-plane and management tokens. If inspection is unavailable, OmniHarness may report the process but may not signal or adopt it. If no valid process exists and the integration is enabled, `src/instrumentation.ts` mirrors its existing `ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted().catch(...)` pattern to schedule a bounded background start. App boot is not blocked by release downloads, OAuth, or an external network probe.\n\nExternal mode never starts, stops, signals, or modifies the external process or config.\n\n## Server-owned state machine\n\nGateway state is not a second test-only observability surface. The singleton produces one complete snapshot with a monotonic `revision`; the operational GET returns it, and the same redacted summary is included in the canonical `/api/events?snapshot=1` payload. All decisions still travel as named frames on the existing SSE ring buffer with IDs and replay behavior:\n\n```text\nmode: managed | external\nenabled: boolean\ninstallation: absent | installing | installed | unsupported | error\nservice: stopped | starting | running | unreachable | error\noauth: disconnected | connecting | connected | error\noperation: null | { id, kind, state, error? }\nmodels: { custom, discovered, updatedAt?, stale }\n```\n\nLegal transitions include:\n\n- `absent -> installing -> installed`\n- `stopped -> starting -> running`\n- `running -> stopped`\n- `disconnected -> connecting -> connected`\n- any active transition to its specific `error` state\n\nRepeated install and start requests share the same in-flight promise. A stale probe may not overwrite a later revision. Cached models may be displayed, but they do not prove service readiness. OAuth completion polling is server-owned and updates this same state/event stream; the browser does not create a competing source of truth.\n\n## API\n\nThe runtime-registry route and Next adapter expose:\n\n```text\nGET  /api/integrations/claude-model-gateway\nPOST /api/integrations/claude-model-gateway\n```\n\nGET returns the complete redacted status snapshot. POST accepts one action:\n\n- `install`\n- `start`\n- `stop`\n- `connect`\n- `refresh_models`\n\nAuthentication is required. Mutations enforce same-origin checks. Inputs are schema-validated and unknown fields/actions are rejected. `connect` returns the OAuth URL and state; the UI opens it and retains a visible fallback link. The server owns bounded completion polling and emits the result through the canonical status/event path.\n\nThe generic settings POST continues to own draft configuration such as mode, external URL, tokens, and custom models. Operational actions are immediate and visually separate from Save/Cancel settings semantics.\n\n## Provider and model clients\n\nThe client uses bounded requests to:\n\n- check readiness;\n- `GET /v1/models` with the data-plane token;\n- request a Codex OAuth URL from the management endpoint;\n- inspect management auth files to recognize OAuth completion.\n\nThis OAuth store is intentionally separate from `src/server/supervisor/codex-auth.ts`, which reads `~/.codex/auth.json` for the supervisor's own Codex fallback. OmniHarness does not copy or reuse those credentials: CLIProxyAPI owns its provider auth directory and token refresh. UI copy calls this the **gateway provider connection** so it is not confused with the existing Codex CLI account.\n\nThe client parses only required response fields and preserves the original error cause internally. It never logs tokens, OAuth URLs containing sensitive query data, or auth-file contents.\n\nModel refresh validates, trims, deduplicates, and caches returned IDs. Custom IDs reject control characters, empty values, duplicates, and oversized input. Installation seeds `gpt-5.6-sol` as a custom model so it remains selectable even before discovery succeeds.\n\nThe agents catalog merges native Claude models, encoded custom models, and encoded cached discoveries. Catalog reads never probe an external service. Source and staleness remain available to the settings status UI.\n\n## Worker routing\n\nBefore any rows are created, conversation/prewarm entry points call `prepareClaudeGatewayLaunch()` for a routed model. It validates the compound selection, checks readiness, and returns a request-fenced prepared selection containing the encoded durable model, raw runtime model, `credentialSource: \"gateway\"`, and sanitized connection metadata. No secret is persisted in that selection. If preparation fails, the request returns before creating a plan, run, worker, message, or artifact.\n\nImmediately before transport, `spawnAgent()` and `prewarmWorker()` call the same helper themselves (deduplicating the readiness check). This covers callers that currently assemble base environments independently. The helper:\n\n1. Recognizes and decodes `cliproxyapi:<raw-model>`.\n2. Loads decrypted gateway settings.\n3. Ensures the selected managed service is ready, or probes the configured external service.\n4. Refuses the spawn with a stable surfaced error if readiness fails.\n5. Marks the runtime request `credentialSource: \"gateway\"` and supplies the required process-only environment:\n\n```text\nANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway base URL>\nANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<data-plane token>\nANTHROPIC_MODEL=<raw model ID>\nCLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=<raw model ID>\nCLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1\nCLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY=3\nENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false\n```\n\n6. Adds the officially documented Claude Code gateway variables `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION=<raw model ID>` and `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1` only when a parsed installed Claude Code version meets the documented minimum capability table (`/v1/models` discovery requires 2.1.129+). These are gateway usability settings, not part of the user's literal alias contract; an unknown/older version leaves them out without weakening the required route.\n7. Sends the raw model ID to the agent runtime while retaining the encoded selection in durable OmniHarness state.\n8. Persists the effective encoded model, effort, and launch credential source on the worker row at reservation time, before background spawn begins. Resume, quota recovery, reconciliation, observer recovery, failover, planning review, and prewarm use that worker-level selection when one exists; legacy rows fall back to the run selection.\n\nInside the agent runtime, `credentialSource: \"gateway\"` is accepted only for `type=\"claude\"`, `accountId=null`, and a routed request prepared by the server. That path skips credential-profile/account/keychain bridging, applies project-scoped storage, then overlays the gateway environment last before computing the pool fingerprint and spawning `claude-agent-acp`. This ordering prevents normal Claude credential resolution from deleting or replacing `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Native Claude keeps the existing credential path.\n\nSpawn, resume, recovery, and prewarm use the same helper. Native Claude selections bypass it. There is no fallback or model substitution. Tests enumerate every current `readRuntimeEnvFromSettings()` + `spawnAgent()`/`prewarmWorker()` caller so a newly missed route fails coverage.\n\n## Compound worker selection\n\nA routed Claude model receives credentials from the gateway, not from an Anthropic/Claude account row. To preserve the repository's compound-selection invariant, model compatibility resolution produces and transmits this complete tuple together:\n\n```text\n{ workerType: \"claude\", accountId: null, model: \"cliproxyapi:<id>\", effort: <selected effort> }\n```\n\nThe composer displays the account portion as the derived, non-editable **Gateway provider connection** while a routed model is selected. The server rejects a non-null Claude account combined with a routed model before creating any plan, run, worker, message, or artifact. Switching back to a native Claude model restores the last compatible Claude account through the existing compound-selection Manager. Runs persist the intentional null account together with the encoded model and effort.\n\n## UI design\n\nThe Agents settings panel gets a focused `ClaudeModelGatewaySettings` section built from existing shadcn/ui primitives. The closest official settings shell is `sidebar-13`, but the existing OmniHarness settings dialog already provides that shell; implementation should reuse it rather than install or overwrite a block.\n\nThe section has clear, progressive states:\n\n- Not installed: explanation and **Install and start**.\n- Installed/stopped: **Start**.\n- Running/disconnected: **Connect gateway provider**.\n- Connecting: status plus a reusable sign-in link.\n- Connected: account status, model list, and **Refresh models**.\n- Error: exact actionable error and retry.\n- External: endpoint and secret inputs, connection health, and model controls; no process-management buttons.\n\nOperational buttons act immediately. Mode, endpoint, secret replacements, and custom model edits use the dialog's normal Save/Cancel flow. Saved tokens use existing configured-secret semantics, so an empty field does not erase them.\n\n`ClaudeModelGatewayManager` is the single frontend state owner. It uses operation/request IDs and server revisions so a slower status response cannot overwrite a newer user action. It consumes the existing live-event connection for service changes and performs GET only for bootstrap/manual refresh. React effects may subscribe; they must not mirror authoritative state into component-local state.\n\nAll visible copy and accessibility labels use `t()` and exist in every locale. Status changes use an accessible live region. The layout must work at desktop and narrow settings widths.\n\n## Lifecycle events and errors\n\nTyped named events cover every server decision:\n\n- install started, completed, and failed;\n- service starting, started, stopped, and start failed;\n- OAuth started, completed, and failed;\n- model refresh completed and failed;\n- worker spawn refused because the routed gateway was not ready.\n\nUser-relevant failures also emit `error.surfaced` with stable codes. Reuse generic process codes where their meaning is exact, and add only domain failures that the existing union cannot express:\n\n- `claude_gateway.install_failed`\n- `claude_gateway.oauth_failed`\n- `claude_gateway.model_discovery_failed`\n- `claude_gateway.not_ready`\n- `claude_gateway.unsupported_platform`\n- `claude_gateway.invalid_configuration`\n- `process.spawn.failed` for managed-service start failures\n- `process.stop.failed` and `process.orphaned_after_restart` for owned-process failures\n\nEvery event identifies its operation and relevant run/worker where available. Errors are specific and preserve causes without exposing secrets. Silent returns and bare catches are forbidden.\n\n## Safety and failure behavior\n\n- All network and readiness operations are bounded.\n- Release assets ar…5363 tokens truncated…sion emits a named event; every user-relevant failure also emits `error.surfaced` with a stable code and meaningful surface.\n- [ ] Preserve complete error stacks/causes internally while sanitizing public snapshots and events.\n- [ ] Hook `src/instrumentation.ts` by mirroring the existing one-line `ensureSupervisorRuntimeStarted().catch(...)` boot pattern after database readiness: schedule adoption/start only when managed and enabled, do not block app boot, and surface failure.\n- [ ] Include the same redacted gateway summary in the live and persisted `/api/events?snapshot=1` builders. ## Codex progress · 2026-07-13T10:16:11.850Z

A major isolation problem is confirmed: the new uppercase gateway settings flow through the existing “all uppercase settings become worker environment” path. That exposes both gateway tokens—including the management token—to native workers and also adds them to unrelated worker pool fingerprints. I’m checking whether tests catch this and whether recovery or UI paths introduce additional release blockers.

Before publishing the terminal run state, the server synchronously\n+cancels volatile and durable wakes, clears wake leases, and resolves every open\n+recovery incident with its normal named event. Otherwise a later sync or timer\n+still owns permission to reactivate the run. Once cancelled, the run rejects\n+late live-worker snapshots from the interrupted turn even when the provider\n+continues reporting `working` briefly.\n+\n+Conversation deletion follows the same ownership rule. Before deleting a\n+worker or run, enumerate and delete every row that references it, including\n+credential allocations and token usage. Route tests must insert a row in each\n+worker-referencing table so new foreign keys cannot silently make deletion\n+partial or impossible.\n+\n+### Rule 12: dependent selections cross the boundary together\n+\n+Worker type, account, model, and effort are one compound composer selection.\n+The value shown in the composer, sent to prewarm, and submitted to conversation\n+creation must come from the same compatibility resolution. A raw account id\n+from a previously selected worker type is not an explicit preference for the\n+new worker.\n+\n+Run selection restores the whole compound selection, including the account.\n+Optimistic run snapshots must carry the same selection fields as the durable\n+run so selecting a newly created conversation cannot replace an explicit\n+account with `auto` before the authoritative snapshot arrives.\n+\n+The server still validates every explicit account selection, but it does so\n+before creating plan, run, worker, message, or artifact state. Rejections use\n+the original client error status and emit `error.surfaced` with a stable code;\n+they never leave a partially created conversation for snapshots to discover.\n+\n ---\n \n ## Anti-patterns to refuse on sight\n \n These are the specific shapes of code that produce the bugs in this document.\n Reviewers should reject these on sight.\n \n 1. **Silent early returns in server methods.**\n    ```ts\n    if (hasLeftoverState) return; // ← BUG\n    ```\n    If a method refuses to proceed, it emits an event explaining why.\n \n 2. **try/catch that swallows.**\n    ```ts\n    try { await doThing(); } catch { /* ignore */ } // ← BUG\n    ```\n    Either rethrow, or emit `error.surfaced` with the context. Never both\n    silent and continuing.\n \n 3. **Client-side derivation of server decisions.**\n    If the server decided something (plan is ready, recovery gave up), the\n    server emits the event. The client does not re-derive it. If the client\n    is computing `derivePlanningStatus()` from raw fields, that is a missing\n    server event.\n \n 4. **SSE frames without `id:`.**\n    Every frame has an id. No exceptions.\n \n 5. **State diffs as the primary observability mechanism.**\n    \"The UI will figure out what happened by diffing snapshots\" is not an\n    observability strategy. Name the event.\n \n 6. **Fault injection inside production code paths.**\n    `if (process.env.CHAOS) throw new Error(\"boom\")` does not appear in\n    server code. Chaos is a client-side concern.\n \n 7. **Tests that boot Chromium to assert on control-plane behaviour.**\n    Use the HTTP/SSE harness. Reserve Playwright for actual UI behaviour\n    (rendering, input handling, layout).\n \n 8. **DELETE handlers that don't enumerate dependent rows.**\n    If a row has foreign-key dependents, the DELETE handler either deletes\n    them in a transaction or emits `conversation.delete_failed` with the\n    blocking table/row. ## Codex progress · 2026-07-13T10:23:56.468Z

The first two security blockers have now been partly addressed in the shared tree: gateway control settings are filtered from worker environments, and installed binaries get an ownership/hash marker; the process command matcher also became exact and start-time-aware. I’m rechecking the revised code now. The remaining high-risk areas are gateway child environment isolation, failover ordering, post-spawn cleanup, and the server state machine’s restart/race behavior.

## Codex final · 2026-07-13T10:27:02.947Z

Verdict: **not production-ready**. The current tree still has four critical gateway issues.

### Critical

- [process-manager.ts:170](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/process-manager.ts:170) launches CLIProxyAPI with `process.env`, exposing unrelated OmniHarness/provider credentials to the third-party binary. Build a minimal child environment containing only required OS variables such as `PATH`, `HOME`, temp, locale, and Windows system variables.

- [worker-failover.ts:323](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/supervisor/worker-failover.ts:323) tears down the outgoing worker before gateway compatibility/readiness is checked. It then uses the run selection instead of the outgoing worker’s saved selection at line 332, and the preparation call at line 335 is outside the failure handler. A routed Claude failover to another worker type can throw after teardown, without a terminal `worker.failover_failed` event, leaving recovery pending. Check compatibility before teardown and park the run cleanly when no routed replacement exists.

- [ClaudeModelGatewayManager.ts:34](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/app/home/ClaudeModelGatewayManager.ts:34) rejects lower revisions, but the server revision resets when the backend restarts at [index.ts:97](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/index.ts:97). After SSE reconnect/resync, the browser can reject the new server’s status indefinitely. Add a server epoch/ownership token or reset gateway state explicitly on `stream.resync_required`.

- [index.ts:72](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/index.ts:72) puts the original, unredacted error in `Error.cause`. Node’s error inspection prints causes, so boot logging in [instrumentation.ts:18](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/instrumentation.ts:18) can expose tokens. The new failure test confirms the secret appears in inspected output. Use a sanitized cause at any thrown/logged boundary.

### Important

- [index.ts:152](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/index.ts:152) only serializes duplicate actions of the same kind. `start`, `stop`, `connect`, and `inspect` can overtake each other; the new test shows `stop()` runs before an in-progress start completes. Use one serialized mutation queue and revision-fence probes.

- Managed inspection at [index.ts:195](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/index.ts:195) equates an owned live PID with a healthy service. It neither probes readiness nor restores OAuth state from `auth-files`, so an unavailable service appears running and a persisted provider login appears disconnected after restart. The new tests expose both failures.

- The service has no shutdown operation or registered bounded shutdown handler. Also, [process-manager.ts:170](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/process-manager.ts:170) can leave a detached child running if start-time inspection or `process.json` writing fails before the cleanup block begins. Validate metadata before spawning and cover every post-spawn step with cleanup.

- [settings.ts:85](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/runtime/http/routes/settings.ts:85) stores gateway mode, URL, and model JSON through the generic settings route without gateway schema validation. Invalid saved values can break status/catalog requests. Validate the complete gateway draft before any writes. Also, [index.ts:256](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/index.ts:256) requires a management token even for external data-plane readiness; only OAuth management actions should require it.

- [client.ts:89](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/client.ts:89) accepts any OAuth URL scheme, while [ClaudeModelGatewaySettings.tsx:50](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/components/settings/ClaudeModelGatewaySettings.tsx:50) opens and renders it. Require safe HTTP(S), preferably HTTPS except loopback. The global Manager also never clears the OAuth URL after completion/failure/stop, and the UI ignores `status.operation.error`, so SSE-reported timeout failures lose their actionable message.

- Gateway refusal events are usually unscoped: [worker-env.ts:90](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/worker-env.ts:90) supports run/worker IDs, but [bridge-client/index.ts:569](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/bridge-client/index.ts:569) does not map `name` to `workerId`. The configured `claude_gateway.invalid_configuration` and `process.orphaned_after_restart` codes are unused in gateway paths. Unexpected exits, adoption refusal, readiness recovery, and shutdown need named decisions.

- The lifecycle scenario does not prove routing end-to-end. [claude-model-gateway-routing.test.ts:16](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/tests/lifecycle/scenarios/claude-model-gateway-routing.test.ts:16) mocks `spawnAgent`, so the fixture’s `/v1/messages` recorder is never exercised. It also omits restart/resume, cached encoded selection, replay/resync, and exact environment checks. UI tests are source-text checks rather than render/interaction tests.

- Claude capability handling is unreachable in production. [worker-env.ts:44](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/src/server/integrations/claude-model-gateway/worker-env.ts:44) supports the 2.1.129 discovery variables, but no production caller supplies `claudeCodeVersion`, so they are always omitted.

- The process log is opened for unlimited append with no ownership/symlink check, rotation, bounded tail, or redaction. Installation is safer now, but copying the binary and writing its marker are not atomic; marker-write failure leaves an unowned version directory that future retries refuse.

### Minor

- Every non-English locale currently contains English gateway copy, for example [de.json:616](/Users/masterman/NLP/omniharness/shared/locales/de.json:616).
- The lifecycle architecture scenario catalog does not list the new gateway scenario.
- Failed installation archives are deleted despite the design saying they remain diagnosable.

### Verification

- Earlier focused run: 17 files, 111 tests passed, including the lifecycle scenario.
- Fresh focused process/service run after new regression tests: **6 failures** covering child environment isolation, secret-bearing causes, action serialization, managed readiness, OAuth restoration, and shutdown.
- Fresh `pnpm typecheck`: fails on the new unimplemented `parentEnv` and `shutdown` expectations.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The worker-settings leak, binary ownership/hash reuse, and exact PID command/start-time checks were improved during review. The critical items above remain.
